problems.title: Does the sorted Schmidt basis minimize nonlocal magic?
problems.detail: An exact answer would turn an optimization over all local bases into an evaluation on the entanglement spectrum.
problems.question: For every bipartite pure state of qubits, does the sorted computational-basis Schmidt representative minimize the stabilizer 2-Rényi entropy over independent local unitaries?
problems.decisive_test: Arbitrary rank and local register sizes are required for the full conjecture. A strictly lower entropy for a state on the same local-unitary orbit would refute it.

problems.title: First priority · A 43-gate Golay preparation
problems.detail: Direct reduction of the two-qubit gate cost of preparing an error-correcting code state. The full depth/count frontier is a larger question.
problems.question: Can the logical zero of the 23-qubit quantum Golay code be prepared with at most 43 CNOT gates, on exactly 23 qubits, with free single-qubit Clifford gates, no measurements and no ancillas?
problems.decisive_test: One explicitly reconstructed circuit with a signed-stabilizer verification in cyclic coordinates answers yes. A no requires a lower bound over all allowed circuits. Failed local searches establish neither a lower bound nor optimality.

problems.title: Exact approximation of quantum transport costs
problems.detail: Computes the optimal operator-norm error for approximating one quantum transport cost by lower-exponent observables.
problems.question: For 0 < p ≤ 1 < q, is the polygon bound exact for every finite spectrum and attained by a single exponent-one function of the observable?
problems.decisive_test: A proof for all finite spectra or one certified counterexample to either prediction settles the stated conjunction. A failed monotone fit alone is insufficient. A strict distance failure requires a bound against the full cut cone.

problems.title: Undistillable entanglement
problems.detail: Separates two fundamental notions of usable entanglement. Answering it requires reasoning about all copy counts or all candidate states.
problems.question: Does there exist a bipartite state with negative partial transpose from which no entanglement can be distilled using any finite number of copies?
problems.decisive_test: A strict negative witness would settle distillability of the specified state at that copy count. The overarching existential question would remain open. Nonnegative samples and coordinate-support classifications leave even the finite-copy target unresolved.

problems.title: Wigner–Husimi inequality
problems.detail: The conjectured sharp bound would connect heterodyne statistics to Wigner negativity and the sampling overhead of quasiprobability simulation. The statement is recent; its long-term standing is unknown.
problems.question: For every single-mode state, is the Wigner L1 norm at most the squared integral of sqrt(Q) divided by 8 pi, with equality exactly for coherent states?
problems.decisive_test: A single state with a rigorously positive residual would refute the universal inequality. Floating point can nominate it; original normalization, explicit quadrature error and tail bounds must then be verified. No violation in a family gives no proof of the universal statement.

problems.title: A lower bound for symmetrized quantum partition functions
problems.detail: This would bound a quantum partition function using symmetrized products of two noncommuting positive matrices.
problems.question: For all finite-dimensional Hermitian H,K and positive integers n,m, is the mean trace of words with n factors exp(H) and m factors exp(K) at least Tr exp(nH+mK)?
problems.decisive_test: The catalogue lower bound quantifies over all finite dimensions and both word counts. A proof in dimension three with three second factors is partial.

problems.title: Optimal check weight for twelve physical qubits encoding three
problems.detail: Measures the lightest possible largest parity check while encoding three logical qubits and detecting every Pauli error of weight up to three.
problems.question: What is the minimum possible maximum generator weight of a binary [[12,3,4]] stabilizer code, over all codes and generating sets?
problems.decisive_test: An independent rank-nine commuting basis of maximum weight six with exact distance four attains six. The quantum weight-enumerator constraints and two exact rational dual identities exclude nine weight-at-most-five stabilizers in any eligible code, including degenerate groups.

problems.title: Optimal check weight for twelve physical qubits encoding four
problems.detail: A distance-four code storing four logical qubits achieves seven-qubit parity checks, fewer than the eight used by the tabulated construction.
problems.question: What is the minimum possible maximum generator weight of a binary [[12,4,4]] stabilizer code, over all codes and generating sets?
problems.decisive_test: An independent rank-eight commuting basis of maximum weight seven with exact distance four attains seven. Two rational dual identities bound the number of stabilizers with support at most six by six or two according to parity, covering degenerate codes as well.

problems.title: Optimal check weight for ten qubits encoding two
problems.detail: Determines how light the checks can be for a ten-qubit, two-logical-qubit, distance-four binary stabilizer.
problems.question: What is the minimum possible maximum generator weight of a binary [[10,2,4]] stabilizer code, over all codes and generating sets?
problems.decisive_test: The Grassl code attains six. Over every graph-state parent from the Danielsen–Parker classification including disconnected products, the distance-compatible rank-eight subspaces have no nonidentity stabilizers of weight at most five. Every eligible group extends to a graph-state parent up to weight-preserving equivalence.

leads.title: Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, and a Moduli-Space Route from Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory
leads.detail: Full identification of the sextic potential within a specific gauge-theory moduli dynamics remains open and is formulated as a research program.

leads.title: A Quantum Model from the Riemann-Siegel Formula
leads.detail: Whether every analytic zero in the lower half of the critical strip belongs to the physical spectral family remains open.

leads.title: Improved two-way capacity upper bounds for amplitude-damping channels
leads.detail: It improves established benchmarks over broad parameter ranges, while the exact entanglement of the generalized resources remains open.

partial_results.title: Two energy levels suffice for both refined trace bounds
partial_results.detail: Both bounds hold in every finite dimension and at all word lengths whenever either observable has at most two distinct levels, with arbitrary multiplicities. The general lower bound remains open.

partial_results.title: Rank-seven nonlocal magic on three qubits per party
partial_results.detail: All rank-seven spectra on two three-qubit registers, three larger-register regions and an unbounded-rank family with only two exceptional amplitudes in the full equal-register list (including zeros) have proofs. Separate project reviewers checked the reductions and exact certificates. External review is pending.

partial_results.title: Photon-number mixtures
partial_results.detail: The written proof covers all photon-number distributions. Lean checks the arithmetic induction.

partial_results.title: The zero–one-photon qubit
partial_results.detail: The proof covers pure and mixed states in the two-level optical subspace.

partial_results.title: Rényi-order obstructions
partial_results.detail: The paper excludes orders and derives a sharp lower threshold on the optical qubit.

partial_results.title: Two-level superpositions
partial_results.detail: The proof covers the convex hull of states supported on at most two Fock levels chosen from zero through five. Coherent superpositions on three or more levels remain outside this case.

partial_results.title: Cubic gates up to 0.15
partial_results.detail: An interval certificate covers a continuum of weak cubic gates with arbitrary Gaussian processing.

partial_results.title: Coordinate support conditions
partial_results.detail: The parity theorem characterizes positive coordinate compressions. Its companion table checks the construction; for three copies the maximum is max(8, 2d) in all dimensions d ≥ 2. Rank-two distillability remains open.

activity.title: A lower bound for symmetrized quantum partition functions
activity.detail: 4 recorded attempts. No counterexample was found. I first held K fixed at the previous witness and tested all 120 ordered choices of four distinct diagonal numerators for H from {−24,−8,0,8,24}, at (n,m)=(5,7). Every numerical gap was positive. I then tested 540 pairs of symmetric tridiagonal matrices at (6,6). The selected pair had the smallest numerical gap relative to Tr exp(6H+6K) in that search, about 4.34×10⁻¹¹.
